properties.description:
* WHAT...Flooding caused by excessive rainfall is expected.

* WHERE...Apache County in northeastern Arizona...

* WHEN...Until 845 AM MDT Friday.

* IMPACTS...Flooding of creeks and normally dry washes is imminent or
occurring.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- At 848 PM MDT, local law enforcement reported flooding in the
Chinle area. Flooding is ongoing or expected to begin shortly.
Chinle Creek is expected to experience flooding northward to Rock
Point.
- This includes the following creeks, washes and rivers...
Black Mountain Wash, Muerto, White Water Wash, Lukachukai Creek,
Chinle Creek, Tezinie Wash, Black Rock Canyon and Sheep Dip
Creek.
- Some locations that will experience flooding include...
Chinle, Many Farms, Rock Point, Canyon De Chelly National
Monument, Many Farms Lake and Mummy Cave Overlook.
- This includes Highway 191 between mile markers 455 and 459...and
between mile markers 462 and 471...and between mile markers 485
and 500.

This includes the following recreation areas andcampgrounds...
Tsegi Overlook, Junction Overlook, White House Overlook, Antelope
House Overlook, Face Rock Overlook and Spider Rock Overlook.
- Additional information is available at weather.gov/flagstaff.
properties.instruction:
Turn around, don't drown when encountering flooded roads. Most flood
deaths occur in vehicles.

Be especially cautious at night when it is harder to recognize the
dangers of flooding.

properties.headline: Severe Thunderstorm Warning issued October 22 at 8:43PM MDT until October 22 at 9:45PM MDT by NWS Albuquerque NM
properties.description:
SVRABQ

The National Weather Service in Albuquerque has issued a

* Severe Thunderstorm Warning for...
Northwestern Los Alamos County in north central New Mexico...
South Central Rio Arriba County in north central New Mexico...
Central Sandoval County in north central New Mexico...

* Until 945 PM MDT.

* At 843 PM MDT, a severe thunderstorm was located 10 miles west of
San Ysidro, or 25 miles northwest of Rio Rancho, moving northeast
at 30 mph.

HAZARD...60 mph wind gusts and small hail.

SOURCE...Radar indicated.

IMPACT...Expect damage to roofs, siding, and trees.

* Locations impacted include...
Cuba, Jemez Springs, San Ysidro, Fenton Lake State Park, Jemez
State Monument, Jemez Pueblo, Zia Pueblo, Regina and Gallina.

This includes Highway 550 between Mile Markers 16 and 74.
properties.instruction:
Seek shelter inside a well-built structure and stay away from
windows. This storm is capable of producing damaging winds.

Wind damage with this storm will occur before any rain or lightning.
Do not wait for the sound of thunder before taking cover. Seek
shelter immediately inside a sturdy structure and stay away from
windows.

Invest 97W continues to develop over the northern Marshall Islands,
centered near 11N166E in the vicinity of Bikini and Rongelap Atolls.
97W is now the subject of a Tropical Cyclone Formation Alert (TCFA)
by the Joint Typhoon Warning Center (JTWC), meaning it is expected
to develop into a significant tropical cyclone (a tropical
depression) within 24 hours. Himawari visible satellite imagery this
afternoon shows numerous showers and isolated thunderstorms across
the northern Marshall Islands, focused mainly over the
northwesternmost islands and atolls. Scatterometry data from this
morning shows fresh to strong west winds near Ujae and Ebadon Atolls,
and surface observations on Kwajalein Island are showing fresh west
winds with frequent strong gusts. Near-gale force gusts have been
observed with passing showers, and significant boat damage was
recently reported along west-facing exposures of Kwajalein as well.

Surging west winds are expected to continue across the western and
central Marshall Islands, south of Invest 97W's center, and boats
should be safely moved from west-facing exposures and secured, if
possible. Fresh to strong west winds will begin to shift
southwesterly tonight as 97W strengthens, and persist through Sunday
as 97W begins to lift north out of the RMI. Locally heavy showers
will be possible across the northern half of the Marshall Islands
through the weekend. Showers and winds will begin to diminish Sunday
night as 97W pulls farther away, but elevated west to southwest swell
associated with the disturbance may persist into early next week.
Elevated surf along west and south reefs may become hazardous this
weekend into early next week as these swells persist. This situation
will be closely monitored for additional impacts to the Marshall
Islands.

For more information on Invest 97W, see bulletins issued by JTWC
under WMO header ABPW10 PGTW.

properties.areaDesc: Cibola, NM; McKinley, NM; Sandoval, NM
properties.headline: Flash Flood Warning issued October 22 at 8:25PM MDT until October 22 at 11:00PM MDT by NWS Albuquerque NM
properties.description:
At 825 PM MDT, Doppler radar indicated thunderstorms producing heavy
rain across the warned area. Between 2 and 4 inches of rain have
fallen. Additional rainfall amounts of 1 to 2 inches are possible in
the warned area. Flash flooding is ongoing or expected to begin
shortly.

HAZARD...Life threatening flash flooding. Thunderstorms producing
flash flooding.

SOURCE...Radar indicated.

IMPACT...Life threatening flash flooding of creeks and streams, urban
areas, highways, streets and underpasses.

Some locations that will experience flash flooding include...
Marquez, Cebolletita, Seboyeta, Bibo, Paguate and Encinal.
properties.instruction:
Turn around, don't drown when encountering flooded roads. Most flood
deaths occur in vehicles.

In hilly or mountainous terrain there are numerous low water
crossings which are potentially dangerous in heavy rain. Do not
attempt to cross flooded roads. Find an alternate route.

properties.headline: Coastal Flood Advisory issued October 22 at 10:08PM EDT until October 23 at 5:00AM EDT by NWS Key West FL
properties.description:
* WHAT...Saltwater flooding.

* WHERE...Upper and Middle Florida Keys.

* WHEN...Through early Friday morning.

* IMPACTS...Saltwater flooding of low elevation streets and lots
is expected. Some storm drains will overflow, and some
seawalls and docks will be overtopped. Boaters can expect less
clearance under fixed bridges. Motorists should remember that
persistent puddles around the times of high tide are almost
certain to contain a mix of saltwater.
properties.instruction:
If travel is required, allow extra time as some roads may be
closed. Do not drive around barricades or through water of
unknown depth. Take the necessary actions to protect flood-prone
property.
